seoTitle: ClickUp Tutorial for Beginners: Task & Project Setup
metaDescription: New to ClickUp? This beginner tutorial covers workspace setup, tasks, team collaboration, and where the AI features (and their real usage limits) live.
intro: Getting started with a new project management tool can feel overwhelming, and ClickUp has more surface area than most beginners expect. This tutorial walks through what a new ClickUp workspace looks like on first login: the sidebar structure, how a task board fills in, where Docs and AI live, and where automation hides. It's built for someone who has never opened ClickUp before and wants to know exactly what to click, in what order, to go from an empty workspace to a working one.

steps.heading: Get oriented in the sidebar first
steps.body: ClickUp organizes everything from one left-hand sidebar. Home, Inbox, Replies, Assigned Comments, and My Tasks sit at the top as personal views, with All Tasks and More just below. AI Chats gives a shortcut into ClickUp's built-in assistant, and Channels and Direct Messages handle team chat without leaving the app. Spaces is the section that matters most for structure: a starter workspace might already show All Tasks, a general Team Space, a dedicated WEDDING space, and a Project Management space, which shows how loosely or tightly each one can be scoped. Spend the first few minutes here before creating anything. Knowing where Spaces, Channels, and personal task views live saves backtracking later.

image.caption: ClickUp's Home sidebar with Inbox, My Tasks, and All Tasks up top, AI Chats and Channels in the middle, and separate Spaces (Team Space, WEDDING, Project Management) listed at the bottom.

steps.heading: Create and manage tasks on a Board
steps.body: Inside a Space, the Board view lays out status columns left to right: To Do, Planning, In Progress, At Risk, Update Required, and On Hold in a typical setup. A task card such as "Design Home Page Layout" carries an assignee avatar, a date range, and a priority flag marked High, all visible without opening the task. Every column has its own "+ Add Task" control, so moving work through stages is just dragging a card or creating one directly where it belongs. This board view is where day-to-day project management happens. It gets more daily use than any dashboard or list.

image.caption: A Board view with status columns for To Do, Planning, In Progress, At Risk, Update Required, and On Hold, showing one task, "Design Home Page Layout," with a due date range and a High priority flag.

steps.heading: Keep notes and docs next to your tasks
steps.body: ClickUp Docs live in the same workspace as the tasks they describe, organized as Pages that can nest. A "Project Notes" doc might hold separate pages for Project 1 and Project 2, each editable inline with a title, a "Start writing" prompt, and quick-insert options for a blank wiki, a table, a column layout, or an embedded ClickUp List. A doc can link straight into a task, and a task can link straight into a doc, so requirements and meeting notes don't have to live in a separate app. For a beginner, the habit worth building early is writing the plan in a Doc before creating tasks from it, not the other way around.

image.caption: A ClickUp Doc titled "Project 1" with Project 1 and Project 2 listed as pages on the left, and quick-insert options for a table, column, or embedded ClickUp List.

steps.heading: Use comments and channels for team collaboration
steps.body: Collaboration runs through two channels at once. Assigned Comments surfaces every comment where a user has been tagged across all tasks, so nothing gets buried in a thread they aren't watching. Channels behaves like team chat scoped to a Space or a topic, such as a General channel tied to the workspace, and Direct Messages sit next to it for one-on-one conversations that don't need to be public. Because comments live on the task itself, the context of a conversation (what task, what status, what deadline) doesn't get lost the way it can in a general-purpose chat app.

steps.heading: Know what ClickUp's AI includes before you build on it
steps.body: The AI section of the sidebar splits into Ask or Create, Super Agents, and a Connections panel showing usage. ClickUp's own help documentation describes the free Brain AI allowance as a lifetime limit, not a monthly one: Free Forever workspaces get 25 AI uses, or 50 in workspaces with more than 10 members, and that allowance never resets. Separate from it, AI Super Credits power automated features including Super Agents, but buying credits needs a paid plan. A trial workspace showing both a use count and a credit balance is most likely running on a paid trial, not the Free Forever tier. Super Agents is also a recent addition: ClickUp rolled it out in February 2026, so it may not appear in every account yet depending on plan and when the workspace was created. Under Super Agents, the panel offers Create Agent, All Agents, My Agents, and Activity. For a beginner, running an existing agent on a real task teaches more, faster, than building a custom one from a blank spec.

image.caption: The AI panel's Super Agents section, with Create Agent, All Agents, My Agents, and Activity listed, plus a Connections panel showing remaining Brain AI uses and credits.

steps.heading: Connect the tools you already use
steps.body: ClickUp's value multiplies once it connects to the tools already in use. Integrations with Slack and Google Drive let notifications, files, and updates flow in without manual copying. Instead of connecting everything on day one, pick the integration that fixes the biggest current annoyance, usually duplicate notifications, and set that up first. More integrations can wait until the core workspace, Spaces, a Board, a Doc, and comment habits, is already working well.

costNote: Spaces, Boards, Docs, and comments are free indefinitely on ClickUp's Free Forever plan. AI is the one place cost becomes relevant: the free plan's Brain AI allowance is a fixed lifetime number of uses that never refills, and buying additional AI Super Credits, which power Super Agents and similar automated features, requires a paid plan.

troubleshooting.problem: ClickUp Brain says the AI usage limit has been reached
troubleshooting.cause: Free Forever workspaces get a fixed lifetime allowance of AI uses, 25 for workspaces up to 10 people or 50 for larger ones, and ClickUp does not refill it automatically.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to a paid plan to keep using Brain AI, or purchase AI Super Credits if the workspace is already on a paid plan.

troubleshooting.problem: Super Agents doesn't show up in the AI panel
troubleshooting.cause: Super Agents launched in February 2026 as a newer ClickUp feature, so older workspaces or certain plans may not have it yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the workspace is on a current plan and that the app is up to date; the feature is still rolling out gradually across accounts.

faq.question: Is ClickUp free to use for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The Free Forever plan covers tasks, Docs, and a limited amount of AI: ClickUp's help documentation caps free Brain AI use at 25 uses per workspace, or 50 for workspaces over 10 people, as a lifetime allowance that doesn't reset. Buying more AI capacity, including what powers Super Agents, needs a paid plan.

faq.question: Can ClickUp integrate with other tools I already use?
faq.answer: Yes, ClickUp supports integrations with tools like Slack and Google Drive, letting notifications and files flow into the workspace instead of staying siloed.

faq.question: What are Super Agents, and do I need to build one?
faq.answer: Super Agents are autonomous AI agents ClickUp added to the platform in February 2026. Beginners get more out of running an existing agent on a real task first, then building a custom one once they know what the AI handles well.

faq.question: Is ClickUp suitable for both personal and team project management?
faq.answer: Yes. The same Spaces structure that organizes a personal space like "WEDDING" can just as easily hold a full team's Project Management space, so it scales down as easily as it scales up.

faq.question: Where do comments and team chat happen in ClickUp?
faq.answer: Task-level discussion happens in comments on the task itself, surfaced globally under Assigned Comments, while broader team chat happens in Channels and Direct Messages in the sidebar.

verifiedNote: Sidebar layout, Board columns, Docs structure, and the AI panel come from a recorded ClickUp walkthrough. The Brain AI usage limits, the separate AI Super Credits system, and the February 2026 launch of Super Agents were checked against ClickUp's help center in September 2026; ClickUp's help pages returned a 403 to direct fetching, so this relied on indexed excerpts of those specific articles instead of a full page load. That check corrected the original draft, which described a free trial workspace showing both AI uses and AI credits as if that were normal on the Free Forever tier, when credits require a paid plan.
